tone.profile: vintage blues-rock lead with wah and gritty mid push

rig.name: Walter Trout - Marie's Mood - Valeton GP-180

blocks.purpose: Clean up hum and background noise.
Provide mid-forward grit and initial boost for lead lines.
blocks.gap: The Green OD is used to simulate the warm, slightly overdriven character of a Plexi/hot combo preamp tone.

blocks.purpose: Essential for the vintage blues sound and lead sweeps.
Add aggressive mid-range grit and sustain without modern high gain.
blocks.gap: The RAT-style is chosen for its classic, gritty overdrive character, fitting the blues-rock context better than pure fuzz or Muff.

blocks.purpose: Simulate the sound of a classic Marshall/Plexi hot combo, providing necessary mid-focus and breakup.
blocks.gap: The UK 45 is the best fit for the Plexi/hot combo clue, emphasizing mids over modern high gain.

blocks.purpose: Provide the classic British cabinet sound associated with blues-rock.
Fine-tune the tone by slightly boosting the mids and controlling low end/highs to prevent scoop.
blocks.gap: Used specifically to counteract any potential EQ scooping inherent in the signal chain, fulfilling the 'drop scooped' cue.

blocks.purpose: Add subtle movement and width to the lead tone without distracting from the grit.
blocks.gap: Not strictly required, but adds dimension suitable for blues-rock leads.

blocks.purpose: Provide a subtle echo for sustain and depth.
Add natural space and depth to the overall tone.

improvements.summary: Improve cabinet realism and overall vintage character.

proposals.reason: Enhance the classic Plexi/hot combo feel and mid-focus.
proposals.expectedGain: Improved tone depth and vintage character.
